label: Butter sculpture
note: Torma are made of ideally yak butter, dyed, often with flour and milk, hand-moulded as temporary altar offerings at Tibetan New Year.

about.text: Butter shaped into figures. The earliest documented one is from a papal banquet in 1536; American dairy promoters made butter sculptures to compete with margarine from 1890 to 1930, and the Iowa State Fair has shown a butter cow every year since 1911. In Tibetan Buddhism coloured butter torma are altar offerings and lamps burn butter.
